Subject: ACME — follow-up & next steps from today's RAG discovery

Hi Samir and Claire,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from the call
- Goal: Improve search relevance for outbound sales enablement content and reduce hallucinations in RAG responses for product FAQs.
- Biggest constraints: strict latency SLOs (~300ms p50), tight cost targets for embedding+retrieval, and internal compliance audit next quarter.

Suggested immediate next steps (for alignment and quick evaluation)
1) Redwood will run a focused eval based on the prompt set you shared (thanks!) against three candidate model+reranker combos and capture grounding metrics: precision@k, grounding rate, and top-1 hallucination rate.
2) I'll share our benchmark CSV and a JSONL prompt set so you can review and run in-parallel.
3) Short sync next week to choose the reranker and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).

What we'll evaluate (high level)
- Retriever: dense (FAISS HNSW) tuned on your CRM docs + content store. We'll try both 128-d and 768-d embedding configs to trade recall vs cost.
- Reranker: candidate list: (A) tiny cross-encoder (distilbert-cross) for low-latency, (B) mid-sized cross-encoder (rerank-bert-medium), and (C) model-based re-ranking using a 7B instruction-tuned model for semantic scoring.
- Generator model candidates: Llama-2-13B-quant (fast), Redwood-7B-chat (cost-optimized), and Red-Chat-13B-v2 (higher-fidelity).

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (your prompts + expected labels), we'll attach our first-pass CSV results after the run.

Proposed date for next sync: Tue 2026-07-14 (10:00am PT). If that doesn't work, suggest times and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Samir/Claire — quick technical follow-up after the first pass we ran this morning. Attaching the CSV with initial numbers and calling out recommended next steps below.

Initial observations (first-pass) — attached acme_rag_benchmark_results.csv
- Retriever: 128-d dense embeddings (FAISS HNSW) had slightly lower recall (recall@10: 0.72) than 768-d (0.81) but reduced embedding cost by ~45%.
- Reranker: distilbert-cross (option A) gave fastest inference (avg rerank latency 60ms on our hosted infra) with modest precision gains. Rerank-bert-medium (B) improved precision@5 by ~8% over A at a ~2x latency cost. Model-based reranking (C) reduced top-1 hallucination rate by ~12% but pushed end-to-end p95 above 500ms in our hosted baseline.
- Generative quality: Red-Chat-13B-v2 produced the most coherent grounded answers but at higher token cost than Redwood-7B-chat. Llama-2-13B-quant was cost-efficient but had occasional grounding lapses on long-doc context.

Our recommended configuration for an initial pilot (balanced latency + grounding):
- Embedding: 128-d dense (to hit cost targets) with aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated queries.
- Retriever: FAISS HNSW, efSearch tuned to favor recall@5 with reranker backing.
- Reranker: rerank-bert-medium (option B) deployed in a single dedicated pool for critical routes; use distilbert-cross as fallback for burst traffic.
- Generator: Redwood-7B-chat for baseline pilot; enable canary to Red-Chat-13B-v2 for high-risk questions where hallucination reduction is critical.

Grounding metrics to include in the pilot dashboard (we'll populate these):
- grounding_rate: percent of tokens/answers that cite an exact doc span
- precision@k (k=1,5,10)
- top-1_hallucination_rate (human-labelled subset)
- latency_p50/p95 for retriever+reranker+generation
- cost_per_query (USD, incl. embedding + retrieval + rerank + generation)

Next steps
1) We'll upload the benchmark CSV to the Drive and paste the link in this thread (done).
2) Aditya will schedule the Tue 7/14 sync — propose 10am PT.
3) If you approve, we'll spin up the rerank-bert-medium dedicated pool for the pilot and share expected commit and cost delta.

Notes on regressions/quality monitoring:
- We'll run nightly evals against your labelled set (50 queries) and configure regression alerts if top-1_hallucination_rate increases by >3 percentage points.
- We'll also snapshot prompts + contexts on drift to detect prompt-induced regressions when models are rolled/updated.

Link to CSV: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD_acme_rag_benchmarks

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks for the data, Marissa — good starting point. A couple technical clarifications from infra/engineering before we spin up a dedicated pool: 

1) Reranker sizing: rerank-bert-medium will need dedicated GPUs for stable p95; can you confirm target qps for the pilot? If <20 qps we can start with a 2-GPU pool and autoscale on CPU fallback.
2) Caching: we can enable prefix/KV caching in the Redwood runtime, but we'll need a list of high-frequency query templates from Acme to set TTLs. Samir/Claire — can you share your top 200 queries or templates?
3) Metrics ingestion: we'll push grounding metrics to the Acme dashboard; what's your preferred retention (30/90/365 days)? We'll default to 90 days for the pilot.

I'll draft an infra change request and estimated cost delta for rerank-bert-medium + 128-d embeddings and share by EOD.

– Dev
